description: Custom recall-quality and quality scenarios for task.md §7 custom cases
notes: Each scenario uses isolated user/session IDs prefixed with the scenario name.
expected_facts: strings that MUST appear (case-insensitive) in /recall context.
forbidden_facts: strings that must NOT appear in /recall context (hallucination guard).
supersession checks are performed via /users/{id}/memories inspection.
All data is cleaned up via DELETE /users/{id} at end of each test.

scenarios.name: fact_evolution_employer
scenarios.description: Employment supersession: Stripe→Notion across sessions. Recall must return current employer; /memories must show supersession chain.

messages.content: I'm a backend engineer at Stripe.
Nice, Stripe is great!
Big news — I just started at Notion as a PM!
Congratulations on the new role at Notion!

probes.query: Where does this user work now?
probes.notes: Must return current employer (Notion), not stale (Stripe)

scenarios.name: fact_evolution_location
scenarios.description: Location supersession: NYC→Berlin. Same pattern as employer.

messages.content: I live in New York City.
NYC is a vibrant city!
I just moved to Berlin last month — loving it so far!
Berlin is a great city! How are you settling in?

scenarios.name: multihop_pet_city
scenarios.description: Multi-hop: user has a pet named Biscuit and lives in Berlin. Query connects both facts.

messages.content: I have a golden retriever named Biscuit.
Biscuit sounds adorable!
I just moved to Berlin from NYC.
Berlin is a great city!

probes.query: What is the user's dog's name?
What city does the user with the dog named Biscuit live in?
probes.notes: Multi-hop: connects pet (Biscuit) with city (Berlin) for the same user

scenarios.name: opinion_arc
scenarios.description: Opinion evolves from positive to negative. Latest stance must be active; prior stance preserved in chain.

messages.content: I absolutely love TypeScript — it's made my code so much safer.
TypeScript does help catch errors early!
TypeScript generics are getting really annoying lately. Too much boilerplate.
Complex generics can definitely add overhead.

probes.query: How does this user feel about TypeScript?
probes.notes: Current opinion about TypeScript should appear; latest stance in the arc

scenarios.name: noise_resistance
scenarios.description: Queries about topics the user never discussed. Context must not fabricate data about those topics.

messages.content: I work as a data scientist and I love Python.
Python is excellent for data science!

probes.query: What is the user's favorite hiking trail?
probes.notes: No hiking data → context must not fabricate hiking facts. Known user facts (data scientist, Python) may appear.

probes.query: Does the user have any siblings?
probes.notes: No family data → context must not fabricate sibling info.

probes.query: What is the user's credit card number?
probes.notes: Sensitive / never-discussed topic → absolutely must not appear.

cold_session_probe.notes: For a brand-new unknown user_id, context must be empty string.

scenarios.name: cross_session_scoping
scenarios.description: Same user, two sessions: facts from both sessions should be accessible via /recall. Different user: zero bleed.

messages.content: I live in Tokyo.
Tokyo is amazing!
I have a cat named Mochi.
Cute name!
I work at Amazon.
Interesting!

probes.notes: User A cross-session fact from s1

probes.query: What is this user's pet's name?
probes.notes: User A cross-session fact from s2
User A must not see user B's Amazon data (cross-user isolation)
User B must not see user A's Tokyo/Mochi data (cross-user isolation)

scenarios.name: delete_cleanup
scenarios.description: DELETE /sessions keeps cross-session facts. DELETE /users wipes all data.

messages.content: I am a nurse and I live in Madrid.
Madrid is wonderful!
I love cooking Italian food.
Italian cuisine is delicious!

checks.assertion: Memories from s1 (nurse, Madrid) survive. /memories count >= 1.
checks.notes: Session s2 is deleted but its memories were extracted — by design memories are user-scoped and session_id is SET NULL, so they survive.
